scope: Read-only source/heap audit; no browser run or source change. Historical snapshots are from comparison-opt-heaps, preceding final first-round commit.

findings.retainingPath: Host Window -> __JIESHU_CORE_INTENTS (or __JIESHU_INJECT.coreOperationSlots) -> application name -> slot -> cancelled Promise and cancel resolver -> resolver Context -> Promise
findings.reproduction: distinct-name-reproduction.json: actual committed beginOperation creates 1000,2000,...,10000 strongly held keys; destroyApp performs this allocation even for an absent sandbox.
findings.fix: Track uses in the shared slot, acquire for begin/observe, release exactly once on operation completion, and delete only current slot with no remaining users. Preload observing a destroy slot must keep it alive until idle preload completion. Promise identity prevents ABA after revision reset.
risks: A completed superseded work release must not delete a replacement slot.
The cancellation-facing completion and actual destroy teardown completion are different for reentrant destroy; release after actual work.
Older separately bundled core copies do not understand lease increments; mixed protocol versions require explicit compatibility handling or scope statement.

A speculative fulfilled Promise.race -> returned destroy callback retention chain was NOT reproduced: actual helper experiment collected all100 markers while intent slots remained. Do not claim sandbox leak on that basis.

findings.kind: confirmed empty weak-table backing capacity after realm GC
findings.retainingPath: Core module lexical Context @105221 -> ka (instanceofPatchStates) WeakMap @105825 -> internal table @108593
findings.attribution: Current standardized build test-results/footprint-bundle/jieshu-whole-core-es2018.js maps ka.get/set usage to registerInstanceofPeer and constructor/peers state. Historical minified Context has same variable ka. Table has only holes and map edge, no live constructor/state entry.
fixOptions: Bind state metadata to the existing patched Symbol.hasInstance function, which already closes over the state, eliminating a module-wide WeakMap table; preserve original-constructor/subclass checks, reference counts and release ownership.
Partition by realm using WeakMap<Window,...> so a collected realm also releases its inner table; audit aliased/shared constructor identity across realms before adopting.

If lifecycle cleanup is chosen, wire the currently ignored release callback into real destroy and verify table capacity actually shrinks; deleting peers alone is insufficient evidence of backing-store release.
findings.expectedCeiling: This historical table itself costs32788 bytes, about8% of407159-byte total self-size delta; not the dominant code/source delta.

findings.interpretation: idToSandboxMap, teardownById and unmountHookDepthById tables are empty; event map contains only host public bus. Core destroy removes sandbox cache and settles/removes tombstones. setupApp options intentionally persist, as Wujie does.

findings.kind: normal fixed module allocations; low priority
findings.interpretation: Three AssetCache objects eagerly create18 Map/WeakMap/WeakSet containers, which are empty after clear except weak-table holes; five document/location membership Sets duplicate information also retained in policy arrays; single-instance forwarding/pipeline classes add fixed objects and closures. Lazy creation can improve never-started baseline but cannot reduce used-then-destroyed idle footprint without discarding state. Pure-function simplification/deduplication is safer than adding lazy/reset machinery for a few KiB.

limitations: Self sizes are not retained sizes or browser RSS.
No new browser memory sampling in this audit.
The previously established258216 code-byte and86015 external-string-byte deltas still dominate; fixing the concrete small state issues cannot guarantee Wujie parity.
Existing V8 weak-table capacity is a collectible-key/capacity issue, not evidence of retained child realms.
